exercises.heading: Section 6.2 Exercises

problem.paragraph: True or False? Line integral $$\int_{C}^{}{f(x,y)ds}$$ is equal to a definite integral if C is a smooth curve defined on $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ and if function $$f$$ is continuous on some region that contains curve C.

True or False? Vector functions $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }_{1} = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ $$0 \leq t \leq 1,$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }_{2} = (1 - t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + {(1 - t)}^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ $$0 \leq t \leq 1,$$ define the same oriented curve.
True or False? $$\int_{-C}^{}{(Pdx + Qdy) = {\int_{C}^{}{(Pdx - Qdy)}}}$$
True or False? A piecewise smooth curve C consists of a finite number of smooth curves that are joined together end to end.
True or False? If C is given by $$x(t) = t, y(t) = t \text{, 0} \leq \text{t} \leq 1,$$ then $${\int_{C}^{}{xyds = {\int_{0}^{1}{t^{2}dt}}}}.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, use a computer algebra system (CAS) to evaluate the line integrals over the indicated path.

problem.paragraph: $$C: \mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 4t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3t\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ when $$0 \leq t \leq 2$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C ( x - y ) d s = 10 \int C ( x - y ) d s = 10$$

problem.paragraph: $$C: \mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \sin t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \cos t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 8t\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ when $$0 \leq t \leq \frac{\pi}{2}$$
[T] Evaluate $${\int_{C}^{}{xy^{4}ds}},$$ where C is the right half of circle $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 16$$ and is traversed in the clockwise direction.

solution.paragraph: $$\int C x y 4 d s = 8192 5 \int C x y 4 d s = 8192 5$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Evaluate $${\int_{C}^{}{4x^{3}ds}},$$ where C is the line segment from $$(-2,-1)$$ to (1, 2).

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find the work done.

problem.paragraph: Find the work done by vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3xy\mathbf{ \text{j} } - (x + z)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ on a particle moving along a line segment that goes from $$(1,4,2)$$ to $$(0,5,1).$$
Find the work done by a person weighing 150 lb walking exactly one revolution up a circular, spiral staircase of radius 3 ft if the person rises 10 ft.

Find the work done by force field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = - \frac{1}{2}x\mathbf{ \text{i} } - \frac{1}{2}y\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \frac{1}{4}\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ on a particle as it moves along the helix $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ from point $$(1,0,0)$$ to point $$\left( {-1,0,3\pi} \right).$$

Find the work done by vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 2x\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ in moving an object along path C, the straight line which joins points (1, 0) and (0, 1).

Find the work done by force $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = 2y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3x\mathbf{ \text{j} } + (x + y)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ in moving an object along curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \cos (t)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \sin (t)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \frac{1}{6}\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ where $$0 \leq t \leq 2\pi.$$
Find the mass of a wire in the shape of a circle of radius 2 centered at (3, 4) with linear mass density $$\rho(x,y) = y^{2}.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, evaluate the line integrals.

problem.paragraph: Evaluate $${\int_{C}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = -1\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ and C is the part of the graph of $$y = \frac{1}{2}x^{3} - x$$ from $$(2,2)$$ to $$(-2,-2).$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r = 4 \int C F \cdot d r = 4$$

problem.paragraph: Evaluate $${\int_{\gamma}^{}{\left( {x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}} \right)^{-1}ds}},$$ where $$\gamma$$ is the helix $$x = \cos t,y = \sin t,z = t(0 \leq t \leq T).$$
Evaluate $$\int_{C}^{}{yz dx + xz dy + xy dz}$$ over the line segment from $$(1,1,1)$$ to $$(3,2,0).$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C y z d x + x z d y + x y d z = -1 \int C y z d x + x z d y + x y d z = -1$$

problem.paragraph: Let C be the line segment from point (0, 1, 1) to point (2, 2, 3). Evaluate line integral $${\int_{C}^{}{yds}}.$$
[T] Use a computer algebra system to evaluate the line integral $${\int_{C}{y^{2}dx + xdy}},$$ where C is the arc of the parabola $$x = 4 - y^{2}$$ from (−5, −3) to (0, 2).

solution.paragraph: $$\int C ( y 2 ) d x + ( x ) d y = 245 6 \int C ( y 2 ) d x + ( x ) d y = 245 6$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Use a computer algebra system to evaluate the line integral $$\int_{C}^{}{\left( {x + 3y^{2}} \right)dy}$$ over the path C given by $$x = 2t, y = 10t,$$ where $$0 \leq t \leq 1.$$
[T] Use a CAS to evaluate line integral $$\int_{C}^{}{xydx + ydy}$$ over path C given by $$x = 2t, y = 10t,$$ where $$0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C x y d x + y d y = 190 3 \int C x y d x + y d y = 190 3$$

problem.paragraph: Evaluate line integral $${\int_{C}^{}{\left( {2x - y} \right)dx + \left( {x + 3y} \right)dy}},$$ where C lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0 \text{to} x = 5.$$
[T] Use a CAS to evaluate $${\int_{C}^{}{\frac{y}{2x^{2} - y^{2}}ds}},$$ where C is $$x = t, y = t, 1 \leq t \leq 5.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C y 2 x 2 - y 2 d s = 2 ln 5 \int C y 2 x 2 - y 2 d s = 2 ln 5$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Use a CAS to evaluate $$\int_{C}{xyds,}$$ where C is $$x = t^{2},y = 4t,0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

exercises.paragraph: In the following exercises, find the work done by force field F on an object moving along the indicated path.

problem.paragraph: $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = -x\mathbf{ \text{i} } - 2y\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x, y) = 2x\mathbf{i} + y\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$
C: counterclockwise around the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (1, 0), and (1, 1)
$$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x, y, z) = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } + y\mathbf{ \text{j} } - 5z\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$
$$\textit{C}: \mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 2 \cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 2 \sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t\mathbf{ \text{k} }, 0 \leq t \leq 2\pi$$

Let F be vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \left( {y^{2} + 2xe^{y} + 1} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {2xy + x^{2}e^{y} + 2y} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Compute the work of integral $${\int_{C}^{}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where C is the path $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \sin t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \cos t\mathbf{ \text{j} }, 0 \leq t \leq \frac{\pi}{2}.$$

Compute the work done by force $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = 2x\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3y\mathbf{ \text{j} } - z\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ along path $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + t^{3}\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ where $$0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

Evaluate $${\int_{C}^{}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = \frac{1}{x + y}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \frac{1}{x + y}\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and C is the segment of the unit circle going counterclockwise from $$(1,0)$$ to (0, 1).

Force $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = zy\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x\mathbf{ \text{j} } + z^{2}x\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ acts on a particle that travels from the origin to point (1, 2, 3). Calculate the work done if the particle travels:

list.item: along the path $$(0,0,0)\rightarrow(1,0,0)\rightarrow(1,2,0)\rightarrow(1,2,3)$$ along straight-line segments joining each pair of endpoints;
along the straight line joining the initial and final points.
Is the work the same along the two paths?

problem.paragraph: Find the work done by vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3xy\mathbf{ \text{j} } - (x + z)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ on a particle moving along a line segment that goes from (1, 4, 2) to (0, 5, 1).

How much work is required to move an object in vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3x\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ along the upper part of ellipse $$\frac{x^{2}}{4} + y^{2} = 1$$ from (2, 0) to $$(-2,0)?$$

A vector field is given by $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = (2x + 3y)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (3x + 2y)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Evaluate the line integral of the field around a circle of unit radius traversed in a clockwise fashion.
Evaluate the line integral of scalar function $$xy$$ along parabolic path $$y = x^{2}$$ connecting the origin to point (1, 1).

solution.paragraph: $$\int C x y d s = 25 5 + 1 120 \int C x y d s = 25 5 + 1 120$$

problem.paragraph: Find $$\int_{C}^{}y^{2}dx + \left( {xy - x^{2}} \right)dy$$ along C: $$y = 3x$$ from (0, 0) to (1, 3).
Find $$\int_{C}^{}y^{2}dx + \left( {xy - x^{2}} \right)dy$$ along C: $$y^{2} = 9x$$ from (0, 0) to (1, 3).

solution.paragraph: $$\int C y 2 d x + ( x y - x 2 ) d y = 6.15 \int C y 2 d x + ( x y - x 2 ) d y = 6.15$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, use a CAS to evaluate the given line integrals.

problem.paragraph: [T] Evaluate $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = x^{2}z\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 6y\mathbf{ \text{j} } + yz^{2}\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ where C is represented by $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + \ln t\mathbf{ \text{k} }, 1 \leq t \leq 3.$$
[T] Evaluate line integral $$\int_{\gamma}^{}{xe^{y}ds}$$ where, $$\gamma$$ is the arc of curve $$x = e^{y}$$ from $$(1,0)$$ to $$(e,1).$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int \gamma x e y d s \approx 7.157 \int \gamma x e y d s \approx 7.157$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Evaluate the integral $${\int_{\gamma}^{}{xy^{2}ds}},$$ where $$\gamma$$ is a triangle with vertices (0, 1, 2), (1, 0, 3), and $$(0,-1,0).$$
[T] Evaluate line integral $${\int_{\gamma}^{}{\left( {y^{2} - xy} \right)ds}},$$ where $$\gamma$$ is curve $$y = \ln x$$ from (1, 0) toward $$(e, 1).$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int \gamma ( y 2 - x y ) d x \approx -1.379 \int \gamma ( y 2 - x y ) d x \approx -1.379$$

problem.paragraph: [T] Evaluate line integral $${\int_{\gamma}^{}{xy^{4}ds}},$$ where $$\gamma$$ is the right half of circle $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 16.$$

[T] Evaluate $${\int_{C}^{}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = x^{2}y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (x - z)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + xyz\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ and
C: $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 2\mathbf{ \text{k} }, 0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r \approx -1.133 \int C F \cdot d r \approx -1.133$$

problem.paragraph: Evaluate $${\int_{C}^{}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}},$$ where $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = 2x \sin (y)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {x^{2}\cos (y) - 3y^{2}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and
C is any path from $$(-1,0)$$ to (5, 1).

Find the line integral of $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = 12x^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } - 5xy\mathbf{ \text{j} } + xz\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ over path C defined by $$y = x^{2},$$ $$z = x^{3}$$ from point (0, 0, 0) to point (2, 4, 8).

solution.paragraph: $$\int C F \cdot d r \approx 2 2 . 8 5 7 \int C F \cdot d r \approx 2 2 . 8 5 7$$

problem.paragraph: Find the line integral of $${\int_{C}^{}{\left( {1 + x^{2}y} \right)ds}},$$ where C is ellipse $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = 2 \cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 3 \sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ from $$0 \leq t \leq \pi.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, find the flux.

problem.paragraph: Compute the flux of $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = x^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + y\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ across a line segment from (0, 0) to (1, 2).
Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = 5\mathbf{ \text{i} }$$ and let C be curve $$y = 0,0 \leq x \leq 4.$$ Find the flux across C.
Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = 5\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and let C be curve $$y = 0,0 \leq x \leq 4.$$ Find the flux across C.

Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = -y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ and let C: $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = \cos t\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \sin t\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ $$(0 \leq t \leq 2\pi).$$ Calculate the flux across C.
Let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left( {x^{2} + y^{3}} \right)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (2xy)\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Calculate flux F orientated counterclockwise across curve C: $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 9.$$

Find the line integral of $${\int_{C}^{}{z^{2}dx + ydy + 2ydz}},$$ where C consists of two parts: $$C_{1}$$ and $$C_{2}.$$ $$C_{1}$$ is the intersection of cylinder $$x^{2} + y^{2} = 16$$ and plane $$z = 3$$ from (0, 4, 3) to $$(-4,0,3).$$ $$C_{2}$$ is a line segment from $$(-4,0,3)$$ to (0, 1, 5).
A spring is made of a thin wire twisted into the shape of a circular helix $$x = 2 \cos t, y = 2 \sin t, z = t.$$ Find the mass of two turns of the spring if the wire has constant mass density.

A thin wire is bent into the shape of a semicircle of radius a. If the linear mass density at point P is directly proportional to its distance from the line through the endpoints, find the mass of the wire.

An object moves in force field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = y^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + 2(x + 1)y\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ counterclockwise from point (2, 0) along elliptical path $$x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 4$$ to $$(-2,0),$$ and back to point (2, 0) along the x-axis. How much work is done by the force field on the object?

Find the work done when an object moves in force field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = 2x\mathbf{ \text{i} } - (x + z)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + (y - x)\mathbf{ \text{k} }$$ along the path given by $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t) = t^{2}\mathbf{ \text{i} } + \left( {t^{2} - t} \right)\mathbf{ \text{j} } + 3\mathbf{ \text{k} },$$ $$0 \leq t \leq 1.$$

If an inverse force field F is given by $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y,z) = \frac{\mathbf{k}}{\left\| \mathbf{ \text{r} } \right\|^{3}}\mathbf{ \text{r} },$$ where k is a constant, find the work done by F as its point of application moves along the x-axis from $$A(1,0,0) \text{to} B(2,0,0).$$

David and Sandra plan to evaluate line integral $$\int_{C}^{}{\mathbf{ \text{F} } \cdot d\mathbf{ \text{r} }}$$ along a path in the xy-plane from (0, 0) to (1, 1). The force field is $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = (x + 2y)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + (-x + y^{2})\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ David chooses the path that runs along the x-axis from (0, 0) to (1, 0) and then runs along the vertical line $$x = 1$$ from (1, 0) to the final point (1, 1). Sandra chooses the direct path along the diagonal line $$y = x$$ from (0, 0) to (1, 1). Whose line integral is larger and by how much?
